name: Raigad Fort
tagline: Shivaji Maharaj's capital — reachable by ropeway or a 1,737-step climb
seoTitle: Raigad Fort Solo Trek Guide — The Solo Trail
seoDescription: Solo guide to Raigad Fort, Shivaji Maharaj's former capital — ropeway vs. the 1,737-step climb, season, safety, and packing.
dataNote: Altitude is cited inconsistently across sources — commonly ~2,700 ft (~820m), though one source cites ~4,350 ft. Treat the higher figure as unverified; confirm locally before publishing a precise number.

seasons.label: Jun – Sep
seasons.sub: Monsoon — greenest views, crowded and slippery on the steps

seasons.label: Oct – Feb
seasons.sub: Clear, comfortable, ropeway makes it accessible year-round

routeOptions.name: Ropeway
routeOptions.notes: Covers most of the ascent; a short walk remains to the main fort area. Best option if traveling solo without trekking gear.

routeOptions.name: Steps from Pachad (Maha Darwaja climb)
routeOptions.notes: ~1,737 steps — the classic approach, popular with fitness-focused solo trekkers.

safety.intro: Raigad is one of the more accessible forts on this list thanks to the ropeway, but the step climb and the Takmak Tok viewpoint both carry real risk if rushed.

alerts.title: Takmak Tok cliff point has no barriers
alerts.body: This lookout point is a genuine sheer drop with no railing. Keep well back, especially with a crowd or on wet stone.

cards.title: Before you go
items: Book ropeway tickets online in peak season to skip queues
Check ropeway operating hours before planning your day

cards.title: On the trail
items: The stone steps get slick and crowded on monsoon weekends — go on a weekday if solo
Carry water — limited vendors once past the ropeway station

cards.title: Solo-specific
items: Very family/tourist-friendly — easy to find people around if you need help
Still respect the unfenced viewpoints even with crowds present

items.name: Camera — the fort complex and views are extensive
